title: Gerald McCoy's NFL Career: Six Straight Pro Bowls in Tampa Bay
question: How many Pro Bowls did Gerald McCoy make after leaving Oklahoma?
answer: Six. Gerald McCoy (OU 2006-09), the No. 3 pick in the 2010 NFL Draft, made six consecutive Pro Bowls with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers from 2012 to 2017 and retired in April 2023 with 59.5 career sacks.
summary: Oklahoma City's Gerald McCoy went No. 3 overall in 2010 and made six straight Pro Bowls for Tampa Bay. Here is the former Sooner's NFL career by the numbers.
body: Gerald McCoy (OU 2006-09) was a hometown hero before he was a Sooner. Born in Oklahoma City, he starred at Southeast High School, redshirted at OU in 2006, then started every one of the 40 games he played for Bob Stoops while twice earning first-team All-Big 12 honors.

In the 2010 draft he went third overall to Tampa Bay, one of three Sooners taken in the first four picks. It took him a couple of seasons to hit full stride, and then he became a Pro Bowl regular: six straight Pro Bowls covering 2012 through 2017, all as a Buccaneer, plus a first-team All-Pro nod in 2013.
His nine seasons in Tampa Bay produced 54.5 sacks and 79 tackles for loss, numbers that place him in the top four in franchise history in both categories.

McCoy spent 2019 with the Carolina Panthers and had five sacks, including 2.5 in a London win over his old Tampa Bay teammates. Injuries kept him off the field for most of his final two seasons with Dallas and Las Vegas, and he announced his retirement on April 14, 2023, at age 35. He finished having started 139 of 140 games played, with 59.5 sacks and 334 tackles, and later joined NFL Network as an analyst.
